## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50, titled *Uyyodhika* ("Seeing an army in action"), is a disciplinary rule in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka governing monastic conduct in the vicinity of armed forces [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that if a monk who is staying with an army goes to observe the army engaged in military action, he incurs an offense of expiation requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic codes. Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-pc50*) and Bhikkhu Parivāra (Pācittiya 50), as well as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga and Prātimokkha versions preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan across the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions, along with the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. Parallel disciplinary injunctions are likewise found in the corresponding nuns' Vinayas, including Theravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 131 and its Chinese and Tibetan equivalents [SuttaCentral]. 

Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 222 matching passages shared with 65 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest Pali-internal reuse occurs with immediately preceding military-related rules, notably Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 48 (sharing §1.6–1.18 with high similarity) and Pācittiya 49 (§1.7–1.18), as well as other procedural segments in Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiyas 78, 13, and 27, and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiyas 41 and 10 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), the Sanskrit *Vinayasūtra*, and the Tibetan *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
